Triage: lands in `domain:ui` (`packages/plugin-chatbot/src/FloatingChatbot.tsx`); rationale: class **(c)** and **(b)**.

**(c)**: an author declares `className` on a `chatbot-floating` node — it **type-checks, parses, and is silently a no-op** on the rendered panel. Authored metadata, silently dropped. **(b)**: the contract is declared and quotable — AGENTS.md #3, *"Always expose `className` in schema props so users can override via JSON"*. ⇒ The escape hatch the convention **requires every widget to expose** is exposed and inert here. `Bug`.

⭐ **The mechanism is language semantics, not an inference**, which is why the static reading suffices for grading: a plain object-literal `className` written **after** `...chatbotProps` in the same JSX element always wins. Each link in the chain is read rather than assumed — the registration destructures `className` as its own named prop, it lands in `chatbotProps.className`, the spread carries it, and the literal `"h-full border-0 rounded-none"` replaces it. ⚠️ The card is scrupulous that this is *"not yet confirmed through a live render"*; ⛔ that gap does not affect the verdict, but the fixing PR should close it with an actual render rather than inheriting the reading.

⭐ And the in-package contrast makes it drift rather than design: `ChatbotEnhanced.tsx` **merges its own `className` with `cn()` throughout**. ⇒ One file in the package overrides where every sibling merges.

`priority:p3`: one node type's styling escape hatch, no data loss, no crash, and the fix is a `cn()` call. ⚠️ Silent, which normally argues up — held at p3 by the narrow blast radius.

⚠️ **The route is a real judgement, ⛔ not a mechanical `cn()`**, and the card names it correctly: `cn(chatbotProps.className, "h-full border-0 rounded-none")` merges everything, but *maybe only specific utility classes should be forced and the rest should merge* — an author who legitimately wants a different border or radius on their floating panel is currently overridden, and after a naive `cn()` would be overridden by CSS ordering instead. ⇒ Decide what the panel genuinely must own versus what an author may replace, and say so in the PR.

⭐ **One thing the card did not flag and the same pass should check: `maxHeight` is the identical shape.** It is also a hardcoded value (`"100%"`) written after `...chatbotProps` in the same element, so an authored `maxHeight` is dropped by the same mechanism. ⇒ Either it is deliberately owned by the panel — in which case say so in a comment — or it is a second instance of this defect. ⛔ Do not fix `className` and leave its twin two lines away unexamined.

⛔ **Not a duplicate and ⛔ not to be merged with the adjacent cards**: objectui#7708's scope is `renderer.tsx`'s *registration-level* spread, one file over, and this predates it on both sides (the raw registration spread never carried `className`, since the registration destructures it out as a named prop). objectui#4425 / #4431 are the `toDomProps` DOM-**leak** family — extra attributes reaching the DOM, the opposite axis from a legitimately-declared prop being overridden after being correctly forwarded.

⭐ Dedup was lit: `chatbot-floating` returns 4 results, so the **0** for the literal panel-fit class string is a reading rather than a dead channel.

⛔ This seat grades and routes only: not claimed, not dispatched, no code.


⭐ CONTROL, in the same package: `ChatbotEnhanced.tsx` calls `cn(` **16** times. ⇒ one file overrides where every sibling merges — drift, ⛔ not design.

## ⛔ THE ROUTE IS A JUDGEMENT AND TRIAGE HANDED IT TO THE DISPATCHING SEAT

Triage is explicit that this is 「a real judgement, ⛔ not a mechanical `cn()`」 and names the trap: the card's own suggestion `cn(chatbotProps.className, "h-full border-0 rounded-none")` **still overrides the author** — by CSS/merge ordering instead of by replacement. So I am setting the boundary rather than passing the fork on:

**The requirement, in terms of outcomes rather than an argument order:**

1. An author who declares a different **border** or **corner radius** on a `chatbot-floating` node **must get it**. Those are aesthetic choices, and AGENTS.md #3's escape hatch exists precisely for them — *"Always expose `className` in schema props so users can override via JSON"*.
2. The panel must still **fit its floating container** when the author declares nothing about size. That is the one thing this element genuinely owns.
3. ⛔ **Do not decide 1 and 2 by reasoning about `cn()`'s semantics. MEASURE them.** Whether this repo's `cn` resolves conflicting utilities by last-wins, by tailwind-merge, or by plain concatenation decides the argument order, and ⛔ I am not asserting which — find out, state the reading, then pick the order that satisfies 1 and 2.
4. Whatever the panel keeps by force, **say so in a comment at the line**, naming why that class is load-bearing. A future reader must be able to tell "owned on purpose" from "written last by accident" — which is the whole reason this card exists.

⇒ If 1 and 2 turn out to be **unsatisfiable together** under this repo's `cn`, ⛔ **stop and report**: that is a ruling about what a floating panel may own, ⛔ not a fix.

## ⭐ `maxHeight` IS THE SAME SHAPE — ⛔ do not fix one and leave its twin two lines up

Triage caught what the card missed: `:84`'s `maxHeight="100%"` is also a hardcoded value written **after** `...chatbotProps` in the same element, so an authored `maxHeight` is dropped by the identical mechanism. ⇒ **Decide it in this pass.** Either it is deliberately owned by the panel — then say so in a comment — or it is a second instance and gets the same treatment. ⛔ Leaving it unexamined is not an option.

## ⚠️ The measurement the card declares it did NOT take — it is yours

The card is scrupulous: *"not yet confirmed through a live render"*. Triage agrees the static reading suffices for **grading** but says the fixing PR *"should close it with an actual render rather than inheriting the reading"*. ⇒ **Drive it.** Author a `chatbot-floating` node with a `className`, render, and assert on the rendered panel's class list — pre-fix it must be missing.

## ⛔ Hard constraints

- ⛔ **Not objectui#7708.** Its scope is `renderer.tsx`'s registration-level spread, one file over, and this defect predates it on **both** sides (the raw registration spread never carried `className`, because the registration destructures it out as a named prop). ⛔ Do not reopen or extend it.
- ⛔ **Not the objectui#4425 / objectui#4431 `toDomProps` family.** That is the DOM-**leak** axis — extra attributes reaching the DOM. This is the opposite: a legitimately declared prop being overridden after being correctly forwarded.
- ⛔ **Do not touch `ChatbotEnhanced.tsx`.** It is the control that shows the convention; it is not the defect.
- ⛔ objectui `AGENTS.md:316`: never `git push --force` or `--force-with-lease`, never push to `main`. Absolute, and ⛔ **not** tiered by seat.

## Clause-②: `no` — a styling merge inside one component; no exported symbol moves and no declarable key is added. ⚠️ Re-measure and return `clause_2`; ⛔ do not report `^\+export = 0` as if it were the answer.

## The pin

Pre-fix red through the **rendered** panel: an authored `className` is absent from the rendered class list. Post-fix it is present **and** the panel's owned class is still there — both halves, or you have measured half the requirement. ⭐ And a control that keeps the fix honest: a node authoring **no** `className` renders exactly what it renders today, so the default face does not move.

## Serial constraints cleared

`packages/plugin-chatbot/src/FloatingChatbot.tsx`. Nothing open touches it; my in-flight cards are objectui#8031 (`plugin-view`/`plugin-list`/`plugin-calendar` fixtures), objectui#8072 (`packages/types`) and objectui#9533 (`plugin-dashboard`, reworking a lint error) — ⛔ no overlap. Merge `main` before opening your PR.

## Return

The measured `cn` semantics and the argument order they dictate, the driven pre-fix red and its post-fix pair, your ruling on `maxHeight` with the comment that records it, the `clause_2` field, and any premise of mine you falsified. **A clean stop is a full success.**

## ⛔⛔ A PREMISE OF MINE FALSIFIED — and it was triage's before it was mine

My order said `maxHeight` is *"the SAME SHAPE"* as `className` and must be ruled in the same pass. Triage said it first: 「`maxHeight` **is the identical shape**…Either it is deliberately owned by the panel — in which case say so in a comment — or it is a second instance of this defect.」

The registration forwards no such prop either (the published height tombstone reads it 1 / 1 / 0 across the three registrations — zero for this one). ⭐ And `className` is the **opposite**: it **is** declared on that face, through `BaseSchema`. That asymmetry is the whole reason one of them was a defect and the other was not, and neither the card, nor triage, nor I had it.

⚠️ Recorded as a lane fact, because this is the second time today: **before calling two adjacent lines "the same shape", check whether the authoring face declares both.** A key that is not declared cannot be dropped.

## The route was decided by MEASUREMENT, and it inverted the card's suggestion

I set the boundary as outcomes and told the lane to measure `cn`'s conflict resolution rather than reason about it. It did — and did it better than I did, through the **rendered** element rather than by reading the helper: the pin's CONTROL case shows `ChatbotEnhanced`'s own `rounded-lg` and `border` **removed from the rendered class list** by the merge with `border-0` / `rounded-none`. ⇒ last-wins, confirmed at the surface that matters.

✅ So the landed order is `cn("h-full border-0 rounded-none", chatbotProps.className)` — **panel first, author last** — the opposite of the card's suggestion, and exactly the trap triage named: author-first would have kept overriding the author by merge ordering instead of by replacement. ✅ Outcomes 1 and 2 are satisfiable together, so ⛔ no ruling about what a floating panel may own was needed.

✅ The pin mounts a `chatbot-floating` node through the **real SDUI host** — `SchemaRenderer` + registry + real portal — and asserts the rendered panel's own class list, found by the `data-obj-id` the host derives from the node id. ⛔ Not a helper's return value, ⛔ not a source grep.

✅ And lint was run with **`pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-chatbot lint`, plain `eslint .`, explicitly NOT `--no-inline-config`** — the instruction I added after a sibling PR went red on precisely that flag an hour ago. 0 errors.

## ⛔ Your clause-② question, ruled: **A — it stays `no`**

You flagged the right boundary and were right not to decide it. The ruling, with the text it rests on:

SKILL.md: 「条款②只指已发布契约面,**拉回已声明契约不触它**」. `className` was **already declared** on this authoring face through `BaseSchema` and **already parsed**; the published faces are byte-unchanged (`ChatbotFloatingSchema` and `FloatingChatbotProps` both); and ⛔ **nothing that was refused before is accepted now**. The accept set does not move in either direction — what moves is whether the renderer *honours* a key the contract already required it to honour, which AGENTS.md #3 demanded in the first place (*"Always expose `className` in schema props so users can override via JSON"*).

⇒ an inert declared key becoming live is **conformance to a contract that already existed**, ⛔ not an extension of it. `needs:contract-review` is correctly absent and I am not hanging it.

⭐ Flagging it rather than assuming it was the right call, and the distinction you drew — *"fills an already-declared field"* — is the one the reference marks as judgement rather than mechanism. That is exactly when to ask.
